To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a short message service–delivered intervention can be effective in reducing HIV risk behaviors among HIV-positive MSM.

1) a short message service–delivered tailored intervention for HIV-positive MSM can be implemented successfully and is well-received; 2) a short message–delivered tailored HIV prevention intervention can reduce HIV-related risk behaviors; and 3) a short message-delivered intervention can increase social support and HIV knowledge.

a tailored, short-message service–based intervention can increase HIV knowledge and social supports among HIV-positive men who use drugs and reduce sexual risk behaviors among HIV-positive men receiving sexual risk reduction messages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an SMS-based intervention to support HIV-positive men who engage in high-risk sexual behavior.

the design, development, implementation, and testing of a short message service (SMS)-based, theory-driven, tailored intervention to support the management of HIV disease among HIV-positive men who use the Internet to find sexual partners (men who have sex with other men [MSM]).

the development and evaluation of a tailored, SMS-based intervention to promote health behavior change in a population that is at high risk of contracting HIV, namely, HIV-positive men who are having sex with men (MSM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study was a proof of concept study and the results showed the feasibility of using a tailored short message intervention to provide ongoing behavioral support for HIV-positive men.
the study was successful in demonstrating the feasibility of the intervention.

a tailored short message–service based intervention designed to provide HIV-positive men who engage in sexual activity with men ongoing reinforcement of risk-reduction behaviors and social support is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of SMS for HIV-positive MSM is a promising approach for increasing HIV knowledge, social supports, and risk reduction behaviors.
the intervention was feasible and effective for increasing HIV knowledge and social supports and reducing HIV risk behaviors.

the use of short message service to deliver tailored, theory-based, and interactive messages is feasible for HIV-positive men and may be effective in reducing risk behaviors and increasing social support.
The main takeaway from our work is that

short message service–mediated behavioral interventions are feasible and acceptable for HIV-positive men, and that these interventions have the potential to be an efficient and cost-effective method for delivering behavioral interventions to this population.
short message service–intervention delivery has potential to be effective and feasible for HIV-positive MSM, and that it can be delivered in an engaging and interactive way.
mobile health interventions can provide an important complement to existing HIV prevention and treatment efforts.
